Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020. These picks span a range of styles—from gritty neo‑noir to high‑stakes heist dramas—and have earned praise from critics and audiences alike.

| # | Title | Director | Key Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|----------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | A sprawling, time‑bending saga that blends meticulous period detail with a deep exploration of loyalty, regret, and the cost of violence. |
| 2 | **Uncut Gems** | Josh and Benny Safdie | Adam Sandler, Kevin Garnett, Jennifer Lawrence | A frenetic, pulse‑pounding look at addiction, risk, and the high‑stakes world of New York’s diamond trade. |
| 3 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Ewan McGregor, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | A courtroom thriller that captures the tension of political dissent and the power of collective action. |
| 4 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | A stylish, fast‑paced caper that balances humor with sharp dialogue and a complex web of betrayals. |
| 5 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological thriller that reimagines the classic horror tale as a tense cat‑and‑mouse chase. |
| 6 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A chilling, character‑driven drama about a man’s descent into paranoia after a false accusation. |
| 7 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily James, David Wenham | A visceral, revenge‑driven narrative set against the backdrop of colonial Australia, blending historical context with intense suspense. |
| 8 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A medieval courtroom drama that turns into a brutal duel, exploring themes of honor, truth, and gender dynamics. |
| 9 | **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A dystopian allegory that uses a vertical prison setting to explore class conflict and human nature. |
|10 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological thriller that reimagines the classic horror tale as a tense cat‑and‑mouse chase. |

### How to Watch

- **Streaming**: Many of these titles are available on major platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, and HBO Max.  
- **Rent/Buy**: Digital rental or purchase options are typically available on iTunes, Google Play, and YouTube Movies.  
- **Physical Media**: Blu‑ray/DVD releases can be found on Amazon or specialty retailers.

Enjoy diving into these gripping crime‑thrillers!
